record.original_question: Obtain reasonable bounds for the Hales- Jewett theorem and for the density version of it.

evidence.quote: Quantitative Hales-Jewett theorem. Obtain reasonable bounds for the Hales- Jewett theorem and for the density version of it. See Section 1 for the discussion on the Hales-Jewett theorem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A combinatorial line in the cube $[k]^n = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}^n$ is a set of $k$ points obtained as follows: fix a string $w \in ([k] \cup \{*\})^n$ that contains at least one wildcard symbol $*$, and for each $i \in [k]$ form the point obtained from $w$ by replacing every $*$ with $i$.

The Hales–Jewett theorem asserts that for every $k \geq 1$ and every $r \geq 1$ there exists an integer $HJ(k,r)$ such that whenever $n \geq HJ(k,r)$, any $r$-coloring of $[k]^n$ contains a monochromatic combinatorial line.

The density Hales–Jewett theorem asserts that for every $k \geq 1$ and every $\delta > 0$ there exists an integer $DHJ(k,\delta)$ such that whenever $n \geq DHJ(k,\delta)$, every subset $A \subseteq [k]^n$ with $|A| \geq \delta k^n$ contains a combinatorial line.

Problem: Obtain reasonable quantitative upper bounds on $HJ(k,r)$ and on $DHJ(k,\delta)$ as functions of their parameters. In particular, determine the correct order of growth of these functions, e.g. whether primitive recursive (or even better) bounds can be achieved for all $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: Shelah (1988) gave primitive-recursive (wowzer-type) bounds for the coloring Hales–Jewett theorem. The Polymath project (2009, published Annals 2012) gave the first elementary proof of the density Hales–Jewett theorem with quantitative bounds: a tower-type bound for $k=3$ and Ackermann-type bounds for $k \geq 4$. Obtaining "reasonable" (e.g. primitive recursive uniformly in $k$, or polynomial/exponential) bounds for the density version remains open.

status_evidence.title: A new proof of the density Hales-Jewett theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Polymath gives an elementary proof of DHJ providing the first quantitative bound on how large n needs to be.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative bounds were obtained by Polymath, but they are tower-type for k=3 and Ackermann-type for larger k.

status_evidence.title: Hales–Jewett theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Shelah's bound for HJ is primitive recursive; density version bounds are much worse.
status_evidence.claim: Improving bounds further remains an active question.
